title: Outlook for iOS and Android: Purview label inheritance from email attachments
summary: The briefing passes: the policy controls, PowerShell calls and licensing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. It accurately reports the disagreement between the launched roadmap item and Learn's mobile support table, and leaves mobile versions and existing-policy rollout behaviour open.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature is sensitivity label inheritance from attachments in Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android will support Microsoft Purview sensitivity label inheritance from attachments.

claims.claim: Outlook can automatically apply an email sensitivity label when users attach sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.claim: Outlook can recommend an email sensitivity label based on labelled attachments.
claims.quote: When users attach files with sensitivity labels, Outlook can automatically apply or recommend an email sensitivity label based on organizational policy settings.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Inheritance is an admin-opt-in policy control enabled by selecting its checkbox.
claims.quote: Turn on email inheritance for when users attach labeled documents to an email message that isn't manually labeled. ... select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: The inheritance checkbox is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Default settings for emails > Inherit label from attachments > Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. For the section Inherit label from attachments, select the checkbox Email inherits highest priority label from attachments.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"} configures automatic attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user. Example: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Automatic"}.

claims.claim: The recommendation option is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > policy > Edit Policy > Default settings for emails > Inherit label from attachments > Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page. ... When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity Global -AdvancedSettings @{AttachmentAction="Recommended"} configures recommended attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: AttachmentAction: Unlabeled emails inherit the highest priority label from file attachments. Set the value to Automatic (to automatically apply the label) or Recommended (as a recommended prompt to the user.

claims.claim: Inheritance is configured per sensitivity label policy.
claims.quote: You configure this setting in the sensitivity label policy, on the Default settings for emails page.

claims.claim: Both policy settings apply to the users and groups to whom the label policy is published.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings. ... When you publish the label policy to your chosen users: ... The policy settings are applied to these users

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: For an email not manually labelled, inheritance dynamically selects from attachment labels published to the user.
claims.quote: With this configuration, a sensitivity label is dynamically selected for the email message, based on the sensitivity labels that are applied to the attachments and published to the user.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Outlook selects the highest priority eligible attachment label when it supports inheritance.
claims.quote: The highest priority label is dynamically selected when it's supported by Outlook.

claims.claim: Inheritance never replaces a manually applied email label.
claims.quote: When an email message has been manually labeled, that label won't be replaced by label inheritance from email attachments.

claims.claim: Inheritance replaces a lower priority label applied automatically or as a default.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.claim: Inheritance does not override a higher priority email label.
claims.quote: Label inheritance from email attachments will replace a lower priority sensitivity label that is automatically applied or applied as a default label, but won't override a higher priority label.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The attachment must be a physical file.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A SharePoint or OneDrive file link does not trigger attachment label inheritance.
claims.quote: The attachment must be a physical file, and can't be a link to a file (for example, a link to a file on Microsoft SharePoint or OneDrive).

claims.claim: The recommendation option becomes available when the inheritance checkbox is selected.
claims.quote: When you select this checkbox, you can then further select the following option: Recommend users apply the attachments label instead of automatically applying it.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: With inheritance enabled, the label is applied automatically unless the recommendation option is selected.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.claim: Users can remove an automatically inherited label or choose a different label before sending, subject to other policy settings.
claims.quote: Without this selection, the label is automatically applied but users can still remove the label or select a different label before sending the email.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: By default, an automatically selected label that applies encryption applies the same encryption to the email.
claims.quote: By default, if the automatically selected label applies encryption, the same encryption is applied to the email.

claims.claim: Learn describes Double Key Encryption cases where inheritance selects no email label or protection.
claims.quote: When Outlook doesn't support DKE: If the highest priority label applies Double Key Encryption, no label or encryption is selected for the email message in Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Learn describes no email label or protection being selected when the highest priority label applies only user-defined Word, PowerPoint and Excel permissions.
claims.quote: If the highest priority label applies just user-defined permissions for Word, PowerPoint, and Excel ... no label or protection is selected for the email message because Outlook doesn't support this label configuration.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels in Outlook for iOS and Android require the mailbox to be hosted in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Windows, Outlook for iOS and Android, Outlook on the web, and new Outlook for Windows, the mailbox must be hosted in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels are not supported for on-premises mailboxes in Outlook for iOS and Android.
claims.quote: For Outlook for Windows, Outlook for iOS and Android, Outlook on the web, and new Outlook for Windows, the mailbox must be hosted in Exchange Online. Sensitivity labels aren't supported for mailboxes that are hosted on-premises.

claims.quote: | Label inheritance from email attachments | Current Channel: 2302+ Monthly Enterprise Channel: 2302+ Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel: 2302+ | Not available | Not available | Not available | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Learn's Outlook capabilities table lists attachment label inheritance as Not available for Outlook on Android.
claims.quote: | Label inheritance from email attachments | Current Channel: 2302+ Monthly Enterprise Channel: 2302+ Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel: 2302+ | Not available | Not available | Not available | Yes | Yes |

claims.claim: Minimum mobile app versions for attachment label inheritance are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android AttachmentAction label inheritance attachments existing policy automatic rollout minimum version. Read sensitivity-labels-versions, sensitivity-labels-office-apps and Exchange mobile sensitivity-labeling guidance; no mobile minimum version found.

claims.claim: Learn's inheritance-setting description does not specifically name iOS or Android or a separate mobile inheritance switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "AttachmentAction" "iOS" "Android" enable policy switch. Read the inheritance section of sensitivity-labels-office-apps, Set-LabelPolicy's AttachmentAction reference and Exchange mobile labeling guidance; no mobile-specific inheritance switch stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing inheritance-checkbox selections take effect on mobile without further action.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android AttachmentAction label inheritance attachments existing policy automatic rollout minimum version. Read roadmap record, Office apps inheritance section, versions table and Exchange mobile labeling guidance; no existing-policy mobile rollout statement found.

claims.claim: No source says inheritance changes existing behaviour for tenants that have not selected the checkbox.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook iOS Android AttachmentAction label inheritance attachments existing policy automatic rollout minimum version; "AttachmentAction" "iOS" "Android" enable policy switch. Read roadmap, Office apps and mobile labeling guidance; no automatic enablement without the policy setting found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Purview service description says sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires Microsoft 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG).

claims.claim: The service-description table includes manual sensitivity labeling in Microsoft 365 E3 and several other plans.
claims.quote: | Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5/E3/A3/G3/F1/F3/Business Premium | OneDrive for Business (Plan 2) | Enterprise Mobility + Security E3/E5 | Office 365 E5/A5/E3/A3 | AIP Plan 1, AIP Plan 2 | ... | Manual Sensitivity Labeling | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Users assigned premium/P2 entitlements must also be assigned standard/Plan 1 entitlements for sensitivity labeling to be available.
claims.quote: A standard/Plan 1 license must be assigned in addition to the premium/P2 license for users to have access to sensitivity labeling for Information Protection for Office 365 and AIP, even if the premium licenses/Plan 2 are assigned.

claims.claim: Using sensitivity labels in Office apps requires a subscription edition of Office.
claims.quote: To use sensitivity labels in Office apps, you must use a subscription edition of Office.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the product's published sensitivity-labeling entitlements, rather than a separately published attachment-inheritance entitlement.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labeling, including automatic or policy-based labeling, requires a Microsoft 365 E5 license or Microsoft 365 Information Protection and Governance (IPG). ... | Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The service description publishes no separate licensing row for email attachment label inheritance.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for attachment label inheritance as of November 2026.
